newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Australian wheat market pressured.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Australian wheat market pressured.

text.p: Australian wheat came under pressure last week from falling international values and uncertainty about the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) pool returns due to be announced later on Monday, the AWB said on Monday.
Regardless of the latest pool price estimate, its harvest payment rate would remain as previously announced, the AWB said in its weekly grain market report.
This sets a rate for Australian Standard White (ASW) at 80 percent of $190 a tonne fob. AWB said this set a floor in the present domestic cash market.
The AWB's wheat indicator price delivered Newcastle fell by A$11.00 a tonne to A$125.75 a tonne over the past week.
The indicator price for durum fell by SA$7.50 a tonne to A$182.50 a tonne.
As earlier reported, the AWB has revised its estimate of the size of the Australian wheat crop to 21 million tonnes from 20 million tonnes.
This reflected increased estimates from all states except Western Australia.

Queensland is now anticipated to produce 1.9 million tonnes (up from 1.7 million), New South Wales 7.0 million (up from 6.5 million), Victoria 2.5 million (up from 2.4 million), South Australia 2.7 million (up from 2.5 million), while the forecast for Western Australia is steady on 6.9 million tonnes.

In the U.S., the discovery of Karnal bunt in the Soft Red Winter wheat country of Tennessee together with fresh European subsidies and more aggressive Argentine sales forced the market lower during the week, AWB said.
In the futures market, all futures came under pressure during the week.
Despite adverse weather the U.S. soy bean crop is improving with yields well above grower expectations.
